summary.text: A carbon tax is a tax charged on the carbon emissions released in producing goods and services.
By raising the price of fossil fuels, it cuts demand for high-emission goods and pushes producers to make them less carbon-intensive.
Rather than setting each polluter's limit, it sets a price and lets market forces find the cheapest way to cut pollution.

facts.label: Tax type
facts.value: An indirect tax on transactions, not income

facts.label: Social cost estimates
facts.value: From around $50 to over $200 per ton

items.prompt: A country adds a carbon tax, and petrol gets more expensive. How is this meant to cut emissions?

options.label: Fuel makers are told exactly how much they may emit
Higher prices lower demand and reward cleaner production
The tax money is spent planting trees by law
Cars are banned on days with high pollution

items.explain: Making fossil fuels pricier reduces demand for high-emission goods and gives an incentive to make them less carbon-intensive.

items.prompt: One government caps each factory's emissions by rule; another charges a fee per tonne and lets factories decide how to respond. What sets the fee approach apart?

options.label: It guarantees an exact total of emissions
It only applies to imported goods
It lets market forces pick the cheapest cuts
It taxes people's income instead of sales

items.explain: Unlike command-and-control rules, a carbon tax sets a price instead of a limit and lets the market find the most efficient reductions.

items.prompt: Critics say a carbon tax hurts families with low or middle incomes most. Why?

options.label: It raises prices of necessities like petrol and electricity
It is collected only from people with low wages
It replaces their income tax with a larger charge
It stops them from buying any imported food

items.explain: The tax can drive up prices of everyday needs such as petrol and electricity, hitting lower-income households hardest.

items.prompt: A government returns the money from its carbon tax to low-income households. What is this kind of policy called?

options.label: Cap and trade
A carbon subsidy
Command and control
Carbon fee and dividend

items.explain: Redistributing carbon tax revenue to low-income groups turns the policy into a carbon fee and dividend.

items.prompt: A carbon tax is meant to also cover methane from farms. How could the tax rate for methane be set?

options.label: By the weight of methane times the coal price
By its warming effect in CO₂-equivalent terms
By how much the farm earns in a year
By charging methane exactly the same as water

items.explain: Other greenhouse gases can be taxed based on their CO₂-equivalent global warming potential.

items.prompt: Two experts disagree on how high a carbon tax should be. Which number is the tax level usually based on?

options.label: The price of a barrel of oil
The country's yearly budget deficit
The social cost of carbon
The average household's income

items.explain: The level of the tax is based on the social cost of carbon, an estimate of the cost of carbon pollution's side effects, whose exact value is debated.
